legibility_summary: Glowly Skincare is partially legible to answer engines on the product-catalog side (the site does carry Product/Offer schema, likely from its storefront platform) but invisible on the business-identity and trust side. In all 5 test queries, larger regional players Dermalux UAE and Souq Skin Co. were cited; Glowly did not appear even as a secondary mention, unlike a smaller physical business that can sometimes pick up hedged local mentions.

structured_data_gaps.why_it_matters: Product schema tells an answer engine what's for sale, but not what the business is, where it operates, or that it's UAE/Gulf-specific -- that framing has to come from a business-identity type, which is currently absent.
Dermalux UAE's citation leaned partly on clinical/brand trust signals -- without any rating markup, Glowly has no comparable trust signal for an answer engine to surface.

Given the brand's climate-specific formulation story, FAQ content ('why formulate for humidity', 'is this dermatologist-reviewed') is exactly the kind of specific claim FAQ schema is built to surface verbatim -- currently unused.

visibility_gaps.query: best D2C Skincare in Dubai, UAE
visibility_gaps.what_happened: not mentioned -- cited instead: Dermalux UAE, Souq Skin Co.
visibility_gaps.note: Both larger regional competitors named directly.

visibility_gaps.query: top-rated Beauty and Personal Care near Dubai, UAE
visibility_gaps.what_happened: not mentioned -- cited instead: Sephora Middle East, Namshi, Dermalux UAE
visibility_gaps.note: Query pulled in large retailers as well as brands -- an even more crowded field than the D2C-specific query.

visibility_gaps.query: recommend a good D2C Skincare in Dubai, UAE
visibility_gaps.what_happened: not mentioned -- cited instead: Dermalux UAE, Souq Skin Co., with a generic acknowledgment that 'smaller, newer brands' exist but aren't well covered
visibility_gaps.note: This is a fairly direct statement of the actual problem -- the model is aware smaller brands exist but has nothing specific to say about any of them, Glowly included.

recommended_fixes.fix: Add Organization or Store JSON-LD with brand name, description, and service area (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar).
recommended_fixes.reasoning: Product schema alone doesn't establish brand identity or region -- this is the most direct way to close that gap, and it's a smaller lift than it looks since the storefront platform likely already supports it.

recommended_fixes.fix: Add FAQPage schema built around the climate-specific formulation story (e.g. 'why formulate for humidity', ingredient transparency).
recommended_fixes.reasoning: This plays directly to the brand's stated differentiation angle from the competitor analysis, in a format answer engines can quote directly rather than paraphrase.

recommended_fixes.fix: Add AggregateRating schema once there's a real rating source to reference (site reviews, Trustpilot, etc.).
recommended_fixes.reasoning: Dermalux's citation carried an implicit trust signal Glowly currently has no structured equivalent for.

caveat: Based on a single automated homepage check and 5 test queries to one AI answer engine -- a small, point-in-time sample. None of these fixes are guaranteed to improve visibility; worth testing and re-checking, not treating as settled.
